title: Model feature similarity gave a small connection prediction gain in one MICrONS split and an uncertain gain in a second
abstract: We tested whether response similarity improves connection prediction for neurons excluded from the connection model training set. We used the public MICrONS functional connectomics v1 edge table from one mouse: 295,371 candidate pairs, 8,128 connected pairs, and 148 selected source neurons. A logistic reference model used axon and dendrite proximity lengths, receptive-field distance, and region and layer labels. Every pair was tested once in each of two neuron partitions. Neither endpoint of a test pair occurred in its training set. In the primary partition, model feature similarity reduced mean log loss by 0.000208 nats per pair, or 0.182%. The conditional 97.5% neuron-score interval was 0.000012 to 0.000405. In a second, exploratory partition, the gain was 0.000176, with interval -0.000039 to 0.000392. Measured movie response similarity had intervals that included zero in both partitions under the two-comparison rule. The gains were small and differed by projection group. The result supports a limited prediction benchmark. It does not establish a general rule across animals. One animal, selected sources, fixed activity features, a single model family, and uncertainty that excludes model training variation limit the result. Code, exact splits, fitted models, pair records, predictions, and checks are supplied.

display.caption: Connection prediction gains in two partitions of the neurons. Bars show conditional 97.5% neuron-score intervals. Positive values favor response similarity. The second partition is exploratory.
